stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist discloses nothing about any patient to anyone. Completed prescriptions sit face up on an open counter and a printed waiting list showing patient names is visible to everyone standing in the queue. No one is shown to have read either of them. What is the position?

choices.text: Compliant, because the pharmacist made no disclosure to any third party.
Compliant, because no one is shown to have read the information on display.
Compliant, provided the pharmacy makes a private consultation area available.
In breach, but only once a patient complains about the arrangement.
In breach, because the duty includes protecting confidential information.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.01(16) requires a licensee to MAINTAIN patient confidentiality AND to PROTECT a patient's confidential information. The second limb is affirmative, so a pharmacist who discloses nothing may still fail the duty by leaving confidential information exposed in the ordinary workflow of the pharmacy.

choice_analysis.A: Non-disclosure answers only the first limb of the duty.
choice_analysis.B: The duty is to protect the information, not to prevent proven reading of it.
choice_analysis.C: A consultation area addresses counselling privacy, not exposed records.
choice_analysis.D: A complaint is not an element of the duty.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the protective limb is breached by the exposure itself.

related_facts: 247 CMR 9.18 separately governs the patient consultation area
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates reduce confidentiality to a rule against telling people things.

reasoning_steps: Separate the maintain limb from the protect limb
Apply the protective limb to the exposed records and list
